details: @gsas/gsas-sdk@99.99.99 is an install-time dependency-confusion package: it publishes version 99.99.99 under a scope that matches a real corporate SDK name, so a private-registry name resolved against the public registry would win. Its only executable content is a preinstall lifecycle hook, an inline `node -e` script in package.json that loads require('dns') and require('os'), builds a DNS name from the installing machine's hostname and the local username (non-alphanumeric characters replaced and lengths truncated), and resolves `<hostname>.<username>.gsas-rce[.]66wdtgr[.]a[.]intrax[.]cc`, swallowing errors. Host and user identifiers therefore leave the host as DNS query labels to an operator-controlled domain at install time. The rest of the tarball is inert: index.js contains only `module.exports = {}`, and the package ships just package.json, README.md and index.js (786 bytes total). The hook does not read environment variables, npm or GitHub tokens,.npmrc, SSH/cloud credential files or file contents, and does not download or execute a second stage. The package describes itself as security research; no repository, license "ISC".

cwes.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
